question: A shopkeeper sells an item for ₹960.4 after giving two successive discounts of 30% and 80% on its marked price. Had he not given any discount, he would have earned a profit of 40%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the item?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discounts of 30% and 80% mean the item is sold at 70% × 20% = 14% of the Marked Price (MP).

0.14 × MP = 960.4 ⇒ MP = ₹6860

If no discount is given, SP = MP = ₹6860.

Profit without discount is 40%, so CP × 1.4 = 6860 ⇒ CP = ₹4900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹960.4

Successive discounts = 30% and 80%

Profit when no discount is given = 40%

**Formula Used:**

MP = SP ÷ [(100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100]

CP = MP ÷ [(100 + P)/100]

**Calculations:**

Let Marked Price be MP.

⇒ MP × (100 − 30)/100 × (100 − 80)/100 = 960.4

⇒ MP × (70/100) × (20/100) = 960.4

⇒ MP × 0.14 = 960.4

⇒ MP = 960.4 ÷ 0.14 = ₹6860

When no discount is given, Selling Price = Marked Price = ₹6860.

Given that profit is 40%, let Cost Price be CP.

⇒ CP × (100 + 40)/100 = 6860

⇒ CP × 1.4 = 6860

⇒ CP = 6860 ÷ 1.4

⇒ CP = ₹4900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts D₁% and D₂% are given successively, the equivalent single discount is given by [D₁ + D₂ − (D₁ × D₂)/100]%.

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed on the article. Any discount is always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price.

No Discount Condition

If no discount is provided by the seller, the item is sold at its Marked Price, meaning Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP).
